newsitem.title: UK: BT, MCI set $10 bln loan for Concert.
newsitem.headline: BT, MCI set $10 bln loan for Concert.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc and MCI Communications Corp on Wednesday announced the arrangers on a $10 billion syndicated credit facility for Concert, BT said in a statement.
Concert is the company formed after the multi-billion dollar merger between BT and MCI.
Bank of America NT&SA, Chase Securities Inc.,Citibank, N.A. and JP Morgan Securities Inc. will serve as arrangers, BT said in the statement.
Citibank, N.A. was named as global coordinator.

"The facility replaces BT's and MCI's current credit facilities and will be used to backstop Concert's commercial paper issuance in connection with post-merger activities and various announced strategic initiatives," BT said.
The $10 billion will be split among a $5.0 billion, 364-day facility; a $2.5 billion five-year facility and a $2.5 billion line of credit facility.
Pricing on the 364-day facility is 2.5 basis points undrawn and LIBOR+10 basis points drawn.
Pricing on the five-year facility is 4.5 basis points undrawn and LIBOR+10 basis points drawn.
The 364-day and five-year facilities each have a utilisation fee of 2.5 basis points when outstandings are in excess of 50 percent of commitments.
